messages.subject: lavaan and censored variables
parts:
I plan to move as many analyses to lavaan as possible (from Mplus, for various reasons). I would like to use this opportunity to send a warm thank to people like Yves Rosseel,  Terrence D. Jorgensen, and Ed Merkle (and many others) for their work on lavaan and associated packages. Your doing the community a great service! 

Obviously, lavaan has been through substantial developments in recent years, but I'm not sure which limitations remain. I found earlier metioning that lavaan does not yet include analyses of censored variables, but failed to find explicit mentioning of such a limitation in later posts or a mentioning of censored variables in lavaan's syntax. 

Is declaring factor indicators (or manifest variables in general) as censored not available in lavaan? And do we have a general overview over limitations in lavaan that cannot be handled by semTools or similar additional packages? 

(Clarification: I would nevertheless run the model in lavaan to increase reproducibility, and in the current analysis not use Bayes/blavaan. But I would include tests with Mplus to check whether  conclusions differ when a very skewed variable is declared as censored.)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan and censored variables
parts: I would like to use this opportunity to send a warm thank to people like Yves Rosseel,  Terrence D. Jorgensen, and Ed Merkle (and many others) for their work on lavaan and associated packages. Your doing the community a great service!
Obviously, lavaan has been through substantial developments in recent years, but I'm not sure which limitations remain.

You can find a list of features and (tentative) plans for future developments on the home page:

https://lavaan.ugent.be/features.html

https://lavaan.ugent.be/development.html
Is declaring factor indicators (or manifest variables in general) as censored not available in lavaan?

No, and highly doubtful.  lavaan's models all assume normality at some level (e.g., normality of latent responses underlying ordinal variables, or ML estimation of continuous data assuming normality, followed by corrections for violations thereof).  Mplus uses numerical integration to estimate models that do not rely on assuming normality (e.g., Poisson or negative-binomial distributed data).  I've seen papers implementing models for censored data in Mplus, that work by creating a binary (over the hurdle or not) and continuous (missing on the other side of the hurdle) copy of each censored variable, but that also requires numerical integration.  Numerical integration is unpardonably slow in R, so it is just not a feasible option.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
